token_endpoint_workarounds.attribution: babelforce's own `AuthController.token()`, read against `specs/babelforce/auth-2026-06-25.openapi.yaml`, which declares no request-side `expires_in`. Recorded from the owner's measurement in flux-exchange's credential-acquisition epic (C-440).
token_endpoint_workarounds.behaviour: `expires_in` is read from the request and defaults to `-1`, which the service reads as *never expires*. An unattended caller that omits it therefore gets a non-expiring token rather than a short-lived one.

token_endpoint_workarounds.attribution: babelforce's own `AuthController.token()`, read against `specs/babelforce/auth-2026-06-25.openapi.yaml`, which declares no request-side `expires_in`. Recorded from the owner's measurement in flux-exchange's credential-acquisition epic (C-440).
token_endpoint_workarounds.behaviour: `expires_in` is read from the request when present, and the service default applies when it is absent.

token_endpoint_workarounds.attribution: babelforce's own `AuthController.token()`, read against `specs/babelforce/auth-2026-06-25.openapi.yaml`, which declares neither a request-side `expires_in` nor `account_id`. Recorded from the owner's measurement in flux-exchange's credential-acquisition epic (C-440).
token_endpoint_workarounds.behaviour: `expires_in` is read from the request and passed into the refresh. Separately, `account_id` on the request **switches the account** the new token belongs to — nothing in RFC 6749 makes a refresh change whose token it is, so a host that rotates a credential without pinning `account_id` can silently move it to another account.

token_endpoint_workarounds.attribution: babelforce's own `AuthController.token()`, read against `specs/babelforce/auth-2026-06-25.openapi.yaml:211-220`, whose `grant_type` enum names four grants and not this one. Recorded from the owner's measurement in flux-exchange's credential-acquisition epic (C-440).
token_endpoint_workarounds.behaviour: A fifth `grant_type` that no vendored document declares at all. `expires_in` is read from the request and then clamped to **at most 60 seconds**, so a lifetime asked for here is a ceiling rather than a request.

token_endpoint_workarounds.attribution: babelforce's own `AuthController.token()`, read against `specs/babelforce/auth-2026-06-25.openapi.yaml`, which declares no request-side `expires_in`. Recorded from the owner's measurement in flux-exchange's credential-acquisition epic (C-440).
token_endpoint_workarounds.behaviour: `expires_in` is **not read**. Only `access_type` is, defaulting to `offline`. This row is a measurement and not a gap: the one grant that ignores the field is the fact a reader most needs, because it is the one where asking for a lifetime silently does nothing.
